I’m farming only 16.1 mu, so I can’t spread myself too thin. With some people working off-farm, I need a plan that is steady and not too labor-heavy. I’ll keep the main part in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that’s what I know best and it gives me two harvests on the same land. But I’ll still keep some cotton, because if grain price is weak, cotton can help balance the income. I won’t chase any fancy method this year. I’ll do roughly what has worked for me before, with a little adjustment on fertilizer and water depending on how the crop looks.

For wheat, I won’t save on topdressing if the leaves look pale, because missing yield on wheat hurts. But I also won’t push fertilizer too hard because cash is tight and irrigation from the well costs money. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is short, so I’ll keep land prep simple and sow quickly after wheat harvest. Cotton takes more watching and more sprays, so I’ll keep it on a smaller area that my family can still manage. My way is practical: not the highest input, not the lowest either, just enough to keep yield stable and risk manageable.
